Senses.PreferredTarget: making a livelihood inside a ghost cave
SearchAliases: doing business in a ghost cave

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Making a livelihood inside a ghost cave pictures sustained business conducted in a dark dwelling of ghosts. Chan masters use it to reject answers and commentaries that settle into mental calculation, blank silence, fixed formulas, or an account that closes rather than answers the living exchange.
EvidenceBody: Chengshan Qia says Fu Dashi’s formulation leads people into ghost-cave work, then supplies a contrasting version.
Yishan’s named heir refuses the charge of emptiness by saying he will never do business there.
Yuanwu Keqin contrasts Xuefeng Yicun’s utterance with conscious calculation and ghost-cave work.
Yuanwu later applies the phrase to closing and opening the hand as if that exhausted the case.
Dahui Zonggao explicitly applies it to taking silence and no-speech as final.
Xuansha Shibei tells a hesitant interlocutor that he knew the man was working in the ghost cave.
Baiyu applies the phrase to the inherited goose-and-water image before giving his own night scene.

Senses.Note: Two hundred twelve exact hits occur in 103 frozen works. Seven independent records preserve criticism of formulation, silence, hesitation, mental calculation, and inherited imagery.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The Zen bend lies in the “livelihood” verb: the cave is not merely visited but made into a settled occupation, and masters level that charge during public adjudication.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The targets of the rebuke vary, so the phrase cannot be reduced to one modern psychological state; its stable fact is sustained work inside the ghost-cave image.
